readme: Localization evidence, one row per canonical feature. `labels` names the design labels this feature renders; a row is `localized` only when every one of them has a Cantonese entry, so this file is checkable against the catalog instead of asserted. The contract test in console/tests/contracts/language-modes.test.mjs recomputes each state from the catalog and fails on any row that disagrees -- a row cannot be marked localized by editing this file alone. English is always the fallback: an untranslated string renders as English rather than as a placeholder or a guess. A not-localized row also carries blockedBy: "not-implemented" when the feature has no implementation to localize, or "no-label-surface" when it is implemented but renders no design label. Those are different amounts of work and a bare not-localized hides both. Localization coverage is therefore capped by implementation coverage, and cannot be raised by translating harder.
